page: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with a constrained vCPU topology. Based on the Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, this instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor using the x86_64 architecture and includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache. The processor features instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and BMI2. Notably, the instance allocates 128.0 GB of system memory, delivering an exceptionally high ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated GPUs are included, but the virtual machine incorporates 644 GB of bundled local SSD storage alongside premium storage capability.

Benchmark measurements reflect the instance's deliberate balance of substantial memory capacity against reduced compute scale. The system achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1279.0 and a multi-core score of 2827.0, with PassMark CPU scoring at 4445.06. Stress-ng tests registered 1411.29 for single-core and 3706.48 for multi-core performance, reflecting the modest physical core count. Memory throughput reached 207.29 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read workloads, while uncached 256 MB reads and writes sustained 27.21 GB/sec and 21.44 GB/sec respectively, corroborated by an average PassMark memory score of 2333.37. Single-threaded compression benchmarks showed reliable throughput with gzip at 24.02 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 9.19 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 3.57 million Redis SET operations per second and static web throughput of 4.03 GB/sec.

The primary operational advantage of the E16-4ds_v4 lies in its constrained-core licensing efficiency. By limiting the vCPU allocation to 4 while preserving the 128 GB memory capacity and 644 GB local SSD of a larger 16-vCPU chassis, organizations can significantly curb per-core database licensing expenditures without sacrificing RAM or fast local scratch storage. The inherent tradeoff is reduced aggregate compute and multi-threaded throughput. This hardware profile is best suited for memory-bound relational databases such as Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle, large in-memory caching layers, and analytical ETL processing where memory footprint is paramount but computational requirements are modest.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on a constrained-core architecture designed to reduce per-core software licensing costs. Powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with 2 physical cores and 4 dedicated vCPUs under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 128 GB of RAM, achieving an exceptionally high 32 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It also integrates a bundled 644 GB local SSD for high-speed scratch space and temporary file operations. Hardware vector instructions including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI support accelerated mathematical workloads. Because compute capacity is intentionally constrained to 4 vCPUs, benchmark results demonstrate modest multi-core compute throughput, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 2827.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 4445.06, alongside 3.57 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance is suited for enterprise relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and analytics engines requiring extensive memory footprints with reduced licensing overhead.
